title: Maths for Post-Quantum Cryptography
subtitle: Lattices, Learning With Errors and the NIST Standards
blurb: Four jurisdictions have put dates on the post-quantum migration; the standards they point at were published in 2024, and the nearest thing to a canonical textbook in 2009. This book closes that gap by building rather than asserting: from modular arithmetic to FIPS 203, 204 and 205 read clause by clause, with 196 exercises, full solutions, and 16 runnable labs whose every numerical claim is tested in continuous integration.

title: Maths for LLMs
subtitle: The Linear Algebra, Probability and Calculus Behind Transformers, Attention and Large Language Models
blurb: Most explanations of large language models show you the code or the intuition; this book shows you the mathematics, with every result derived in full. Scaled dot-product attention and why the scaling factor is 1/√d_k, rotary position embeddings, FlashAttention, DPO from the KL-regularised objective — through to KV-cache footprints and training FLOP budgets from first principles. 180 exercises with full worked solutions and a companion repository where every derivation runs as code.

title: Distributed Systems Thinking
subtitle: Architectural Judgment for the AI-Assisted Engineer
blurb: Fourteen chapters on the part of software engineering that does not transfer to the machine: deciding what a system should be, and being able to say why. Coupling and the architecture quantum, synchronous contracts, event-driven design, resilience and cost, each worked through a single production RAG platform built up across the whole book. It offers no model solutions, only tradeoffs with the price attached.

title: Six Ideas That Run the World
subtitle: The School Maths and Science Behind Rockets, AI, Medicine and Everything Next — Derived in Full, Nothing Skipped
blurb: Six ideas that quietly run the modern world — rocketry, AI, epidemiology, cryptography, GPS and optimisation — derived in full using nothing beyond strong school-level mathematics. Where the real research runs past the syllabus, the book says so plainly and names what you would learn next.

title: Maths for Quantum Computing
subtitle: Linear Algebra, Complex Numbers, Probability and Quantum Algorithms
blurb: A ground-up course on the mathematics behind quantum computing, written for developers who are strong in Python and light on the linear algebra. Every idea is taught NumPy-first, then shown once in Qiskit, with exercises and full solutions.

title: Maths for AI
subtitle: Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability and Optimization for Machine Learning
blurb: A ground-up rebuild of the mathematics behind modern machine learning for people who can code but have not thought seriously about mathematics in years. Linear algebra through SVD and PCA, calculus through backpropagation, probability through maximum likelihood — each shown in runnable NumPy, with companion Colab notebooks.

title: Digital Twins for 6G
subtitle: Fundamental Theory, Technology and Applications
publisher: The Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET)
editors: H. Ahmadi, T. Q. Duong, A. Nag, V. Sharma, B. Canberk, O. A. Dobre
blurb: Brings together industrial practitioners and researchers on digital twin technology and its relationship with 6G — covering fundamentals, enabling technologies, standards and advanced topics, and demystifying the networking requirements and benefits of digital twins for electronic, computer and communications engineers.

title: Intelligent Communication Networks
subtitle: Research and Applications
editors: R. Mahapatra, S. Bhattacharyya, A. Nag
blurb: Traces the evolution of computational intelligence techniques for communication networks — machine learning foundations, resource allocation, spectrum management, channel estimation, the wireless physical layer, and applications to optical networks — for senior undergraduates, graduate students and researchers.
